verdict.rationale: The IRS publishes an exact paper and fax fallback for EIN applications: Form SS-4 mailed to a specific Cincinnati address or faxed to 855-641-6935. That route covers the times the online assistant is closed, limited to one EIN per day, or timed out. For the 83(b) election it also documents a written statement or Form 15620 filed by mail. Missing for 10: an exact 83(b) mailing address in the evidence (it only says the Service Center where you file your return), and independent or hands-on confirmation that the paper and fax routes work.

support.subject: As a founder, a paper, fax, or mail fallback rail is published with the exact addresses, numbers, and forms, so the task can still be completed when the online flow is unavailable

citations.quote: Internal Revenue Service, Attn: EIN Operation, Cincinnati, OH 45999, Fax: 855-641-6935
You can make the choice by filing a written statement, or Form 15620, Section 83(b) Election, with the Internal Revenue Service Center where you file your return.
This tool is available during the following times (Eastern Time): Mon–Fri: 6:00 a.m. – 1:00 a.m. (next day); Sat: 6:00 a.m. – 9:00 p.m.; Sun: 6:00 p.m. – 12:00 a.m.
